classification.difficultyReason: Recognises each lattice path as a sequence of ten independent left-or-right choices.

content.prompt: A drop of water is placed at the top of the grid. The drop must run downwards along edges of the grid. How many different ways can it reach the ground?

spec.sourceRegion: Question 8 lattice beneath the stem, on the left.
spec.description: Triangular diamond lattice with an apex, ten downward edge levels and eleven terminal vertices meeting a ground strip. The source beige ground is represented by house light orange; the irregular strip edge is simplified.
spec.mathematics: At depth r, vertices have coordinates (-r+2j,-r), j=0,...,r. Each vertex above depth 10 has two downward edges to the next level. All paths terminate after exactly ten binary choices.
spec.answerVisibility: The complete unlabelled lattice is permanently visible; no path counts or solution annotations appear.

inlines.text: The water droplet must make a sequence of 10 moves to get to the ground.
Each move can either be left or right.
